scenario: After a short imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a man convicted of reckless driving wants to organise a foundation for young victims of highway accidents. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 125,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim, whose car was damaged, opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I approve and accept the money for the foundation, victims of other accidents will benefit from the 125,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
entities: I,1 man convicted of reckless driving who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,1 victim whose car was damaged and who opposes the foundation,an unknown number of young victims of highway accidents who would otherwise have been potential beneficiaries of the foundation
outcomes: The 125,000 dollars is not donated to the foundation.
Victims of other accidents do not receive help from the 125,000 dollars.
The convicted man does not get a foundation named after himself.
The convicted man does not receive image-repair from the foundation.
The victim whose car was damaged does not have the foundation approved over their objection.
